name: phase0_battery_xcheck
description: Cross-validate RAPL against the battery's own current and voltage sensors
(critique item B1.2). Every power number in this thesis comes from one
software counter, MSR_PKG_ENERGY_STATUS, which on client Intel silicon is
partly modelled. The standing objection is that the operand effect lives in
RAPL's activity model rather than in the die. This answers it with an
instrument that shares nothing with RAPL.
MUST RUN ON BATTERY. On mains current_now reports charge current and there
is no discharge to measure, so the runner needs --allow-battery here (the
one place in the project where measuring on battery is the point, not a
mistake). Unplug the charger before launching.
The harness alternates ws_l3_x8 between the all-zero and all-ones operand on
long interleaved arms -- seconds, not the milliseconds the RAPL driver uses,
because battery telemetry updates ~1 Hz and is coarse -- and over each arm
records BOTH the RAPL package power and the mean battery V*I. If the heavier
operand draws more measured discharge power, by an amount comparable to what
RAPL reports (a little more, since the battery also pays the VRM conversion
loss), the +1.9 W effect is physically real. analysis.battery reports the two
deltas side by side and their ratio.
Config-A so the frequency is pinned and the delta is a power delta, keeping
it comparable to the Config-A RAPL figure -- though the on-battery power
state is its own regime, so only the operand DELTA is compared, never the
absolute watts. The aa_l3 control must read ~zero on both instruments.
Each run is 2 conditions x 20 rounds x ~4.8 s ~= 3.2 min of battery drain;
two labels x two repeats is ~13 min, a few watt-hours.

runs.label: l3_hw32
runs.comment: The +1.9 W effect. Battery must see it too.
